title: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange
description: A sequence diagram of the Diffie-Hellman key exchange: Alice and Bob each keep a private exponent, send public values over a wire Eve can read, and arrive at the same shared secret that Eve cannot recover without solving the discrete logarithm problem.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Trace the steps by which Alice and Bob derive a shared secret over a public channel.
Distinguish which values are public (p, g, A, B) from which are kept secret (a, b, s).
Explain why an eavesdropper cannot recover the shared secret without solving the discrete logarithm problem.
educational.prerequisites: Modular arithmetic basics and the idea of a public vs. private value.

pedagogical.interaction: Static, color-coded, responsive sequence diagram with a public-parameters callout.
pedagogical.assessment: Lesson plan asks students to list what Eve knows vs. what she still cannot compute.
pedagogical.misconceptions: Counters the idea that anything sent on the wire is enough to reconstruct the secret.
